newsitem.title: SUDAN: 10,000 displaced reach Juba in southern Sudan.
newsitem.headline: 10,000 displaced reach Juba in southern Sudan.

text.p: About 10,000 displaced Sudanese and Ugandan and Zairean refugees have taken refuge in the south Sudanese town of Juba from fighting between the Sudanese army and southern rebels, state radio said on Sunday.
The radio quoted Fath al-Rahman al-Gadi, the head of Sudan's Humanitarian Aid Commission as saying his department had allocated 1,000 tonnes of sorghum to feed the newcomers.
The rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army says it is advancing on Juba after capturing the towns of Yei to the southwest and Kajo-Kaji to the south.
Many of the 250,000 people in Juba, southern Sudan's largest town, are themselves displaced from earlier rounds of fighting.
A local member of parliament said last week that tens of thousands of Sudanese civilians had fled to Juba from surrounding areas including Yei.
